# Termivar v0.10.0-alpha.1

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Termivar v0.10.0-alpha.1 is an experimental prerelease. It is not
> production-ready and has not completed an independent security audit. Use it
> only on systems you own or are explicitly authorized to test.

## What this release is

Termivar is a bounded, evidence-driven security assessment platform. This
prerelease establishes its current product identity and packages a deliberately
curated set of Preview capabilities around deterministic execution, explicit
authority, typed evidence, and claim-safe reporting.

## Highlights

- One bounded decision runtime with exact-origin authority and shared request,
  byte, cancellation, deadline, evidence, and completeness accounting.
- Structural SQL and SSTI review and context-aware HTML, attribute, and
  JavaScript XSS review. These produce only the documented evidence and at most
  `NeedsReview`; they do not confirm exploitability.
- Defense observation and bounded normalization-resilience review without a
  generic WAF-bypass claim.
- GraphQL, OpenAPI, and read-only REST surface review. Their surface
  observations are `Informational / KnowledgeOnly`; OpenAPI knowledge does not
  authorize arbitrary operation execution.
- Two-principal resource authorization differential review. Replayed
  equivalence can require review but is not confirmed IDOR, BOLA, or an
  authorization bypass.
- A versioned scanner conformance corpus, explicit local artifact signature
  scanning, and strict CI coverage, architecture, fuzz, security, and
  cross-platform gates. Artifact matches are observations, not malware
  verdicts.
- The exploit foundation remains isolated contract infrastructure, not a
  real-target exploit framework or a library of production exploit/CVE
  modules.

## Included downloadable binary capabilities

The downloadable `termivar` binary uses the non-default `release-bundle`. It
includes the artifact adapter, normalization resilience, GraphQL review,
OpenAPI review, REST read-only review, and resource authorization review in
addition to the CLI's normal bounded scanning and reporting foundation.

The release binary does not include the quarantined legacy scanner, the
unsupported API listener, or the experimental proxy adapter.

## Evidence and claim model

An observation is not automatically a vulnerability. Termivar separates
identity, evidence, authority, disposition, and final claims. SQL, SSTI, and
XSS structural evidence stays within its documented authority; no
browser-backed JavaScript execution confirms XSS. GraphQL, OpenAPI, and REST
surface presence is informational. Authorization equivalence does not prove
the declared policy, exploitability, or business impact. No generic WAF bypass
or automatic vulnerability confirmation is claimed.

## Upgrade from Venom

```text
Former CLI:
venom

Current CLI:
termivar
```

First-party packages moved from `venom-*` to `termivar-*`, Rust crate imports
from `venom_*` to `termivar_*`, active performance environment variables from
`VENOM_PERF_*` to `TERMIVAR_PERF_*`, and active cache/container identity from
`.venom` to `.termivar`. No legacy `venom` binary alias is shipped.

Stable compatibility identities may intentionally retain `venom.*`, related
schema names, and digest domain separators. Historical provenance also retains
the former name. These strings do not represent a second product or scanner.
See the [product migration guide](https://github.com/ITherso/termivar/blob/main/docs/migrations/venom-to-termivar.md)
and the [`ScanContext` migration guide](https://github.com/ITherso/termivar/blob/main/docs/migrations/scan-context-construction.md).

## Installation and verification

Download the archive for your platform and `SHA256SUMS` from this release. On
systems with GNU coreutils, place them in the same directory and run:

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```

On Windows, compare the SHA-256 value returned by
`Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 <archive>` with the matching line in
`SHA256SUMS`. After safe extraction, verify the binary identity and inspect its
available commands:

```bash
termivar --version
termivar --help
```

Termivar crates are not published by this workflow; no package-manager
installation channel is implied.

## Known limitations

- This is an experimental `0.x` prerelease: APIs may change, it has not
  completed an independent security audit, and it is not production-ready.
- The scanner does not perform unrestricted crawling, browser or JavaScript
  execution for XSS confirmation, generic WAF bypass, automatic identifier
  mutation, or broad REST fuzzing.
- No production exploit/CVE modules or real-target exploit adapter are shipped.
- The unsupported API listener, experimental proxy adapter, and legacy scanner
  are excluded from the downloadable binary.
- This workflow does not publish crates, containers, packages, or a website.
